issues.title: Cross-field validation using field_validator incorrectly
issues.description: The validation logic checks both bucket_folder and bucket fields (cross-field validation) but uses @field_validator instead of @model_validator, causing order-dependent validation issues and accessing potentially unvalidated fields via info.data
issues.rule_name: Pydantic Models Must Use model_validator for Cross-Field Validation

issues.title: Incorrect string matching for path prefix detection causes false positives
issues.description: The double-nesting prevention logic uses `self.bucket_folder in path` instead of `path.startswith(self.bucket_folder)`. This causes false positives when bucket_folder appears anywhere in the path, not just as a prefix. For example, if bucket_folder is 'results/' and the path is 'my-results/file.txt', the code incorrectly treats it as already prefixed and returns it unchanged, skipping the necessary path resolution. This breaks the fix for issue #20174 in edge cases where folder names contain the bucket_folder as a substring.

issues.title: Incorrect parameter name prevents timeout configuration in test harness
issues.description: The test fixture uses `server_timeout=60` when calling `prefect_test_harness()`, but the correct parameter name is `server_startup_timeout`. This means the intended 60-second timeout is not actually applied, leaving tests vulnerable to the same timeout issues in CI environments that the change was meant to fix. The prefect_test_harness function will ignore the invalid parameter and use its default timeout value instead, potentially causing intermittent test failures when multiple xdist workers start simultaneously in CI.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
# Increase timeout for CI environments where multiple xdist workers
# start servers simultaneously, which can be slower on Python 3.11+
# See https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/16397
with prefect_test_harness(server_timeout=60):
    yield

issues.title: Test constructs invalid path with double slashes
issues.description: The test constructs `already_prefixed_path = f"{bucket_folder}/abc123"` but bucket_folder always ends with a trailing slash (enforced by the _bucket_folder_suffix validator). This creates paths like 'results//abc123' with double slashes. While the double-nesting prevention logic should handle this, the test no longer accurately simulates the actual scenario described in issue #20174 where paths are already correctly prefixed without double slashes. This makes the test less effective at catching regressions in the double-nesting prevention logic.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
# Simulate path that already has bucket_folder prefix
# (as would happen when create_result_record calls _resolve_path)
already_prefixed_path = f"{bucket_folder}/abc123"

# When write_path calls _resolve_path again, it should NOT double-nest
result = gcs_bucket._resolve_path(already_prefixed_path)

issues.title: Unused import: model_validator
issues.description: `model_validator` is imported but not used anywhere in the modified code (the cross-field validation still uses `@field_validator`). This leaves an unused import in the module.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: from pydantic import Field, field_validator, model_validator
issues.rule_name: Unused Imports Must Be Automatically Removed

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #20177 - fix(prefect-gcp): prevent double-nesting in GcsBucket._resolve_path

structured_output.summary:
This PR tries to stop `GcsBucket._resolve_path` from adding `bucket_folder` twice when a path already has it, which happens when `storage_block_id` is null and the path goes through the resolver twice. It also adds an unrelated validator that rejects a `bucket_folder` equal to the bucket name, adds a regression test, fixes the `.prefectignore` fixture, raises the test-harness server timeout, and changes the pytest warning filters.

The fix doesn't do what it says. The guard checks `self.bucket_folder in path` (is the folder anywhere in the path) rather than `path.startswith(self.bucket_folder)`. Any path that contains the folder string in the middle skips prefixing. For example, with `bucket_folder="data/"`, the path `"mydata/x"` is written to the bucket root instead of `data/mydata/x`. That breaks the folder isolation that reads, writes and directory upload/download all depend on. The new validator changes behaviour that nobody asked for, ships with a self-contradicting comment, and leaves an unused `model_validator` import. The regression test uses an unrealistic `//` path and has no case for the substring false positive, so it can't catch the bug.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The core fix uses a substring check instead of a prefix check. Paths that only contain the folder name are then read from and written to outside the configured `bucket_folder`. The PR also bundles an unrelated validator that can stop existing saved blocks from loading.

architecture.overview:
`GcsBucket` is a Prefect storage block. Every path-based operation (`read_path`, `write_path`, `get_directory`, `put_directory`) goes through `_resolve_path`, which joins the configured `bucket_folder` onto the path the caller passes in. A separate helper, `_join_bucket_folder`, is used by the newer block-interface methods and already skips joining when the path starts with `bucket_folder` (from #18237). When Prefect's result-persistence code runs without a `storage_block_id`, a path can go through `_resolve_path` twice and end up as `results/results/...`.

The PR adds an early return to `_resolve_path` that hands the path back unchanged if it appears to be prefixed already. It also adds a field validator that rejects a `bucket_folder` equal to the bucket name, and makes test-infrastructure changes (harness timeout, warning filters, the `.prefectignore` fixture).
steps: Start at `GcsBucket.write_path` / `read_path` (cloud_storage.py ~880-916): both call `_resolve_path` before calling the GCS upload/download helpers.
`get_directory` and `put_directory` (lines 764, 827) also call `_resolve_path` when the caller gives an explicit path.
`_resolve_path` (lines 715-745) now returns the input path unchanged if it already appears to include `bucket_folder`; otherwise it joins `bucket_folder` onto the path with `PurePosixPath`.
Compare `_join_bucket_folder` (line 919), which uses `startswith` for the same purpose.
The `_bucket_folder_suffix` validator (line 698) now also reads `info.data['bucket']` and raises an error when the folder name equals the bucket name.

diagrams.title: GcsBucket path resolution
diagrams.description: How caller-supplied paths go through `_resolve_path` before reaching the GCS helpers.
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A[write_path / read_path] --> R[_resolve_path]
  B[get_directory / put_directory] --> R
  R --> C{bucket_folder set and path already includes it?}
  C -- yes --> P[return path unchanged]
  C -- no --> J[PurePosixPath bucket_folder + path]
  J --> N{path in '', '.', '/'}
  N -- yes --> X[None = bucket root]
  N -- no --> Y[joined path]
  P --> G[_upload_blob_from_string / _download_blob_as_bytes]
  Y --> G
  X --> G

findings.title: Double-nesting guard uses a substring match instead of a prefix match
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/integrations/prefect-gcp/prefect_gcp/cloud_storage.py`, `GcsBucket._resolve_path` (line 734) uses `self.bucket_folder in path`, which matches the folder anywhere in the path. Paths like `mydata/x` with `bucket_folder='data/'` then skip prefixing and resolve outside the folder. Change it to a prefix check, `path.startswith(self.bucket_folder)`, matching `_join_bucket_folder` at line 928. Then add tests in `tests/test_cloud_storage.py`: a path that contains the folder string in the middle (e.g. `f"other/{bucket_folder}x"`, or `mybase_folder/x` with the `base_folder` fixture) must still be prefixed.

findings.title: Unrelated validator change can stop existing saved blocks from loading
findings.body:
This bug-fix PR also adds a new validation rule to `_bucket_folder_suffix`:

::diff{file="src/integrations/prefect-gcp/prefect_gcp/cloud_storage.py" lines="698-713"}

Problems:
- **Behaviour change:** a bucket named `foo` with a folder `foo/` is a perfectly valid GCS layout. Any saved block document with that configuration will now fail validation on `GcsBucket.load()`, and nothing in the PR offers a migration path.
- The code comment says it "should use @model_validator but incorrectly uses @field_validator". That reads like a note left in by accident, not a design decision.
- `model_validator` is imported at line 10 but never used.
- None of this is in the PR description or tested.

I'd drop this hunk and the import. If the rule is wanted, put it in a separate PR with a `model_validator`, tests and a changelog note.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/integrations/prefect-gcp/prefect_gcp/cloud_storage.py`, revert the cross-field check added to `_bucket_folder_suffix` (lines 700-713): remove the `info` parameter, the comment, and the `ValueError` for `bucket_folder == bucket`. Also remove the unused `model_validator` import on line 10. This rule is out of scope for the double-nesting fix and would stop existing saved blocks from loading.

findings.title: Regression test uses an unrealistic path and misses the substring case
findings.body:
::diff{file="src/integrations/prefect-gcp/tests/test_cloud_storage.py" lines="156-165"}

`bucket_folder` always ends with `/` (the validator guarantees it), so `f"{bucket_folder}/abc123"` produces `base_folder//abc123`. That path never appears in the real flow, where the first `_resolve_path` call yields `base_folder/abc123`.

The test also only checks that the folder is detected. It has no negative case, so it passes with the buggy `in` check. A test for a path that merely contains the folder string (e.g. `mybase_folder/x` or `other/base_folder/x`) would have caught the high-severity bug above.

The second assertion, `not result.startswith(f"{bucket_folder}{bucket_folder}")`, can't fail once the first assertion passes.

A stronger test calls `_resolve_path` twice and checks idempotence: `once = gcs_bucket._resolve_path("abc123"); assert gcs_bucket._resolve_path(once) == once`. Add a parametrized negative case alongside it.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/integrations/prefect-gcp/tests/test_cloud_storage.py`, rewrite `test_resolve_path_no_double_nesting` (lines 143-165). Build the already-prefixed path as `gcs_bucket._resolve_path("abc123")`, not `f"{bucket_folder}/abc123"` (which gives a double slash), and assert that resolving it again returns the same value. Add a parametrized negative test: paths that contain the folder name but don't start with it (e.g. `"mybase_folder/x"`, `"other/base_folder/x"`) must still get the `bucket_folder` prefix. Drop the redundant `startswith` assertion.

findings.title: Warning filters don't match the PR description, and the protobuf filter was dropped
findings.body:
::diff{file="src/integrations/prefect-gcp/pyproject.toml" lines="103-106"}

The description says filters were added for `google.api_core` and `coolname`, but only `httplib2` and `pathspec` are present. The existing `google._upb._message` PyType_Spec filter was also removed without explanation, so that DeprecationWarning will come back on Python 3.12+. No `error` filter is configured, so nothing breaks — it's just noise. Either restore the protobuf filter or explain why it's no longer needed, and bring the description in line with the change.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/integrations/prefect-gcp/pyproject.toml` (filterwarnings, lines 103-106), restore the removed `google._upb._message ... PyType_Spec` ignore unless there's a reason to drop it. Either add the `google.api_core` and `coolname` filters the PR description mentions, or update the description to match.
